parts.name: 3.3 V regulator

name: Jetson Orin Nano
model: NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano Super / P3766
accuracy: Carrier, heatsink, fan, support base, internal sockets and mounting hardware are tessellated from NVIDIA’s official P3766 STEP model in millimetres. External receptacles are reconstructed with open shells at the CAD positions and envelope sizes; their recessed contacts are illustrative. The module is the vendor’s mechanical envelope, not a reconstruction of individual chips. Materials and printed markings are reconstructed. The optional example SSD in the source CAD is omitted. The Super software upgrade uses the same physical developer-kit hardware.

parts.name: Orin Nano compute module
parts.description: The removable Orin Nano module combines the Arm CPU, Ampere GPU and LPDDR5 memory. NVIDIA supplies its package envelope in this CAD assembly; the shapes beneath the cooler show clearance volumes rather than individual silicon packages.

parts.name: Aluminium heatsink
parts.description: The finned heatsink transfers heat from the compute module into the fan airflow. Its cavity, fins and mounting features retain the official NVIDIA CAD geometry.

parts.name: Cooling fan
parts.description: The impeller and motor lift from the heatsink. The blade geometry and motor supports are taken directly from the developer-kit CAD.

parts.name: External connectors

parts.name: 40-pin expansion header
parts.description: The 40-position female header exposes GPIO and peripheral buses. It retains the 2.54 mm pitch and source location along the side of the carrier.

parts.name: Compute-module socket
parts.description: The keyed socket accepts the compute module’s edge contacts. Its retention arms and openings retain the official CAD shapes.

parts.name: Cooler & module fasteners
parts.description: The mounting hardware holds the module and thermal assembly together. The spring clip, screws and standoffs use their original CAD geometry and axes.

parts.name: Fan cable & connector
parts.description: The four-conductor fan cable routes to the dedicated header on the carrier. The cable and plug move as one group.

parts.name: Camera connectors
parts.description: The two 22-position flexible-cable connectors expose the camera interfaces on the opposite edge from the GPIO bank.

parts.name: M.2 expansion sockets
parts.description: Two underside Key-M sockets support NVMe storage, and the Key-E socket holds the wireless module. The optional SSD included as an example in NVIDIA’s CAD is omitted from this stock-kit view.

parts.name: Wireless module & antennas

parts.name: Control header
parts.description: The low-profile control header provides power, reset, recovery and debug connections. It remains a separate assembly from the main 40-pin GPIO bank.

parts.name: SMD components

parts.name: Carrier support base

parts.name: RP2350A microcontroller
parts.description: RP2350A provides two Arm Cortex-M33 cores or two Hazard3 RISC-V cores, with 520 KB of on-chip SRAM. The soldered QFN-60 package occupies the center of the board.

parts.name: QSPI flash memory

parts.name: Wireless shield

parts.name: CYW43439 wireless IC

parts.name: Micro-B USB port
parts.description: The five-contact Micro-B socket powers the board and connects the RP2350 USB 1.1 interface. Holding BOOTSEL during connection exposes the bootloader for drag-and-drop programming.

parts.name: BOOTSEL button
parts.description: Holding BOOTSEL while connecting USB starts the ROM bootloader. It is a boot selection switch, not a dedicated reset button.

parts.name: Power conversion circuit

parts.name: System crystal

parts.name: User LED

parts.name: SWD debug pads

parts.name: SMD components

parts.name: Pico 2 W PCB

name: Arduino Nano
accuracy: The PCB outline, mounting holes, copper, component centers, rotations and contact footprints are extracted from Arduino’s NanoV3.3 EAGLE file. The unpopulated ICSP footprint remains part of the board. This is an educational reconstruction, not a manufacturing model.

parts.name: ATmega328P
parts.description: The classic Nano’s 16 MHz AVR runs the sketch. This V3.3 revision uses a soldered 32-contact VQFN package, not a removable DIP chip.

parts.name: Mini-B USB port
parts.description: The five-contact Mini-B socket supplies USB power and connects to the FT232RL serial bridge on the underside.

parts.name: Breadboard headers
parts.description: Thirty square posts sit on 2.54 mm pitch, with the plastic spacers below the board. The two rows are 15.24 mm apart. They carry power, digital I/O and eight analog inputs.

parts.name: FT232RL USB bridge
parts.description: The FTDI chip converts USB to serial for sketch uploads and serial communication. Its 28 gull-wing leads and underside position follow the official layout.

parts.name: 5 V regulator
parts.description: The linear regulator supplies the 5 V rail when the Nano is powered through VIN. USB power enters through the separate protection circuit.

parts.name: Reset button
parts.description: The tactile button pulls RESET low. It resets the sketch without disconnecting power.

parts.name: 16 MHz resonator
parts.description: A three-terminal ceramic resonator provides the ATmega328P clock. It retains its 45° orientation from the PCB file.

parts.name: Status LEDs
parts.description: The four indicator LEDs show board power, serial receive/transmit activity and the sketch-controlled D13 signal.

parts.name: USB resettable fuse
parts.description: The underside F1 resettable fuse protects the USB supply path. Its position and package come from the official Nano V3.3 layout.

parts.name: USB power diode
parts.description: The D1 Schottky diode belongs to the USB power path. Its original underside footprint and orientation are retained.

parts.name: SMD components
parts.description: The remaining capacitors and resistor networks stay together as one selectable group. Positions and values come from the Nano V3.3 schematic and layout.

parts.name: Nano V3.3 PCB
parts.description: The rectangular PCB includes the original copper routing, four mounting holes and six unpopulated ICSP pads. The CAD outline is 43.18 × 17.78 mm; Arduino quotes a nominal 45 × 18 mm product envelope.

parts.name: 26-pin expansion header

parts.name: Orange Pi 5 PCB

parts.name: microSD socket

parts.name: SPI NOR flash

parts.name: Fan connector

parts.name: SMD components

name: Nikon 24–70mm VR
basis: Documented optical topology · representative internal mechanisms
accuracy: Locked to the Nikon F-mount AF-S NIKKOR 24–70mm f/2.8E ED VR, manual 7MA0196C-03 ©2015, not the older G lens or Z-mount version. Nikon documents 20 elements in 16 optical groups, two ED elements, one ED aspherical element, three other asphericals, one HRI element, nine diaphragm blades, SWM internal focus, electromagnetic aperture and lens-shift VR. name: Blu-ray pickup
accuracy: Locked to the Sony KES-400A specimen marked 1216 / 060905 / 6138 in Leslie Wright and Sam Goldwasser’s first-hand PS3 dissection, with the compatible photographed KEM-400AAA-type optical deck. The original article calls the whole deck KES-400AAA; the catalog assembly name is KEM-400AAA. The 75 mm pickup length is a first-hand measurement, not a Sony dimensional drawing. Other casting, board and deck dimensions are photo-estimated. Counts and order follow the dissection: one five-pin can with three emitters and a monitor detector, two polarizing cubes, two return arrays, a moving collimator, an approximately 4 mm LCD corrector, a negative meniscus doublet, a turning mirror, an unconfirmed-retardance wave plate, and one objective with a separate zone plate. The zone plate’s approximately 48 ring pairs are an observer estimate with at least ±25% measurement uncertainty. Lens profiles, electrode segmentation, suspension dimensions, screw pitch and strokes are representative. Focus ±0.6 mm and fine tracking ±0.4 mm are enlarged teaching motions; the eight-second radial scan and Gaussian return indicator are illustrative, not calibrated servo response. Beam lines explain outgoing and returning roles without solving the optical prescription or data encoding. The disc overlay is a reference medium, excluded from the physical parts inventory. Camera orbit never supplies servo input.

basis: Documented CBA architecture · magnified representative cutaway
accuracy: Locked to the 1 Tb TLC BiCS FLASH generation 8 described by Kioxia on 28 March 2024 and in the cited 2023 VLSI/IEDM work. The 218 word lines, three bits per cell, directly bonded CMOS/array architecture and OPS selection principle are documented. This is an enlarged eight-string section, not a retail package or a complete die. All sizes, layer thicknesses, staircase geometry, routing, displayed contact count and CMOS floorplan are representative; no actual device millimetres or production pinout is asserted. name: SII thermal printer
basis: Documented mechanism and timing · representative hidden gearing
accuracy: Locked to SII LTP02-245-01, technical reference U00128436600, August 2012. Do not substitute newer -13x specifications: this -01 reference allows 90 mm/s maximum and 5.5–8.0 V drive. The 67.3 × 18.1 × 30.0 mm nominal envelope excludes protrusions, and the external drawing separately shows a 32 mm height and flex extension. Platen diameter 6.8 mm, overall shaft span 64.55 mm, gear outside diameter 8.05 mm, 384 heaters at 0.125 mm pitch, 58 mm paper/48 mm print width, 24 flex contacts and 0.03125 mm feed per step are documented. Two 0.0625 mm half-dot activations form each 0.125 mm line after four feed steps. Orange heating highlights are explanatory; the real heater is not visibly incandescent.
